key_insight: Bayesian inverse modeling generates virtual aortic cohorts compatible with prescribed hemodynamic biomarkers rather than identifying a single geometry.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports uncertainty-aware virtual patient generation for aortic coarctation studies constrained by pressure-drop measurements.
method: Encode vascular shape in a high-dimensional latent space and generate aortic surfaces with a conditional LDDMM stochastic interpolant.
Evaluate biomarkers using finite element simulations of unsteady incompressible Navier–Stokes flow.
Compare EAKI, aBUS, and WFR sequential Monte Carlo, introducing a differentiable flow-matching surrogate for the WFR approach.
evidence_signal: The three strategies are validated and compared on synthetic data for cohorts matching prescribed pressure drops in coarcted aortas.
watch_item: The surrogate reduces forward-evaluation cost but introduces distribution shift that depends on its training distribution.
paper_title: Inverse domain uncertainty quantification in hemodynamics: sampling virtual patient cohorts under constraints
